questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.subtopic: First law of thermodynamics; heat and work sign convention
questions.stem: A gas in a piston-cylinder absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. Using the convention that work done by the gas is positive, what is the change in its internal energy?
explanations: The first-law convention here is ΔU = Q − W, so work done by the gas is subtracted: 500 − 200, not 500 + 200.
Correct. Heat added is +500 J and work done by the gas is +200 J, so ΔU = 500 − 200 = +300 J.
The sign is reversed. Because the gas receives more heat than the work it sends out, its internal energy increases.
This would imply a net loss of 700 J, but the gas receives 500 J and transfers only 200 J out as work.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus — p1-03 General Science. OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §3.3, First Law of Thermodynamics: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-2/pages/3-3-first-law-of-thermodynamics

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol adds a phasedown of which group of chemicals, which do not deplete stratospheric ozone but have high global-warming potential?
options: Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
Halons
Methyl bromide
explanations: Correct. The Kigali Amendment adds a phasedown of HFC production and consumption; HFCs are not ozone-depleting but can have high global-warming potential.
CFCs are ozone-depleting substances already controlled under the Montreal Protocol; they are not the new chemical group added by Kigali.
Halons are ozone-depleting substances controlled under the Montreal Protocol, not the specific Kigali HFC phasedown target.
Methyl bromide is an ozone-depleting substance controlled under the Montreal Protocol, not the HFC group targeted by Kigali.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus — p1-04 Environmental issues. Government of India, PMO, Cabinet approval for ratification of the Kigali Amendment: https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-approves-ratification-of-kigali-amendment-to-the-montreal-protocol-on-substances-that-deplete-the-ozone-layer-for-phase-down-of-hydrofluorocarbons/

questions.topic: Physical, Social and Economic Geography and Demography of Telangana
questions.subtopic: Telangana natural vegetation; dry deciduous forests
questions.stem: A field note describes Telangana's natural vegetation as largely deciduous, with teak and species of Terminalia, Pterocarpus and Anogeissus. Which broad forest type best matches the Telangana Forest Department's description?
options: Tropical wet evergreen
Dry deciduous
Mangrove
Alpine coniferous
explanations: Evergreen forests retain dense foliage through the year and are not the broad type identified in the Telangana Forest Department description.
Correct. The State's vegetation is described as largely dry deciduous, with teak and the listed dry-forest genera.
Mangroves are tidal coastal or estuarine forests; Telangana is an inland Deccan state.
Alpine coniferous forests are associated with high mountain environments, not Telangana's broad natural vegetation.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus — p1-07 Geography and Demography of Telangana. Telangana Government, Nirmal District Forest Department: https://nirmal.telangana.gov.in/forest-department/

questions.topic: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana
questions.stem: A Telangana Tourism profile lists Lambadi among the popular dance forms of Narayanpet. Which option correctly identifies Lambadi in this cultural context?
options: A folk dance form associated with Lambadi/Banjara communities
A scroll-painting tradition practised by Cheriyal artisans
A brass inlay craft centred on Pembarthi
A Kakatiya-era warrior dance known as Perini Sivatandavam
explanations: Correct. Telangana Tourism lists Lambadi among Narayanpet's popular dance forms; it is associated with Lambadi/Banjara cultural traditions.
Cheriyal is known for narrative scroll painting, not the Lambadi dance form.
Pembarthi is associated with brassware and metal craft, not Lambadi dance.
Perini Sivatandavam is a distinct Kakatiya-era warrior dance tradition; it is not Lambadi.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus — p1-12 Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana. Telangana Tourism, Narayanpet destination profile: https://tourism.telangana.gov.in/destinations/narayanpet

questions.stem: A level-triggered JK flip-flop has J = K = 1, and the active clock pulse remains high longer than the flip-flop's propagation delay. Which behaviour describes the race-around condition?
options: The output may toggle repeatedly during the same active clock pulse, making its final state uncertain.
The output changes exactly once at the leading clock edge, regardless of pulse width.
Both Q and Q̅ are forced high for the duration of the pulse.
The flip-flop becomes permanently insensitive to J and K after the first toggle.
explanations: Correct. With J = K = 1, feedback can cause repeated toggling while a level-triggered clock remains active longer than the propagation delay; the final state may be ambiguous.
A single transition at a clock edge describes edge-triggered operation, not the race-around behaviour of a level-triggered JK flip-flop.
Q and Q̅ are complementary outputs; race-around does not force both outputs high.
The flip-flop does not become permanently disabled; the issue is repeated state changes within one active clock pulse.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus — p2-04 Digital Logic. IIT Kharagpur Virtual Labs, Synthesis of Flip-Flops: https://coa-iitkgp.vlabs.ac.in/exp/synthesis-flip-flops/theory.html

questions.stem: In a centralized daisy-chain bus-arbitration scheme, two devices request the bus simultaneously. The bus-grant signal propagates serially from the arbiter through the devices. Which requester receives the grant first?
options: The requesting device nearest to the arbiter in the grant chain
The requesting device farthest from the arbiter
The device with the largest memory capacity
The device that issued its request last
explanations: Correct. The grant reaches the first device in the chain first; a requesting device captures it instead of passing it onward.
A farther device receives the grant only if all earlier devices pass it along.
Memory capacity does not determine priority in a daisy-chain arbitration scheme.
The scheme uses fixed physical priority, not last-requested or time-based priority.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus — p2-05 Computer Organization and Architecture. Florida International University, Bus Arbitration: https://users.cs.fiu.edu/~downeyt/cda4101/x-arbiter.htm

questions.subtopic: View serializability; blind writes; precedence graph
questions.stem: Consider schedule S: r1(X), w2(X), w1(X), w3(X). Assume no transaction reads a value written by another transaction. Which statement is correct?
options: S is view-serializable but not conflict-serializable.
S is conflict-serializable but not view-serializable.
S is neither view-serializable nor conflict-serializable.
S is both conflict-serializable and view-serializable.
explanations: Correct. S is view-equivalent to serial order T1, T2, T3: T1 reads the initial value of X and T3 performs the final write. But the conflict graph contains T1→T2 (r1 before w2) and T2→T1 (w2 before w1), so it has a cycle.
The cycle T1→T2→T1 means the schedule is not conflict-serializable; conflict-serializable schedules are view-serializable, not the reverse in every case.
The schedule is view-equivalent to T1, T2, T3 because its read-from and final-write relationships match that serial order.
The precedence graph is cyclic, so the schedule cannot be conflict-serializable even though it is view-serializable.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus — p2-11 Databases. IIT Kharagpur, Database System Concepts, Concurrency Control, View Serializability: https://cse.iitkgp.ac.in/~ksrao/pdf/dbms-23/ch18.pdf; Cornell CS4320 concurrency-control slides: https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs4320/2008fa/slides/20081031_cc.pdf

questions.stem: In classic Ethernet's binary exponential backoff, a station has experienced three collisions on the same frame. Which range of integer slot counts may it choose for the next backoff?
options: 0 or 1 slot
0 through 3 slots
0 through 7 slots
0 through 15 slots
explanations: This is the range after the first collision, not the third.
This is the range after the second collision, not the third.
Correct. After the i-th collision, the station chooses K from 0 through 2^i − 1 (subject to the exponent cap); for i = 3, the range is 0 through 7.
0 through 15 is the range after the fourth collision, not the third.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus — p2-13 Computer Networks. ANU Centre for Distance Education, Computer Networks, Ethernet and Binary Exponential Backoff: https://anucde.info/material/202MC24.pdf

questions.subtopic: XML Schema; simple-type restriction and facets
questions.stem: An XML document must restrict an <age> element to an integer value from 18 through 60 inclusive. Which XML Schema Definition (XSD) mechanism expresses this numeric range constraint?
options: An xs:simpleType restriction of xs:integer using xs:minInclusive and xs:maxInclusive facets
An xs:sequence compositor listing child elements in order
A DTD #PCDATA declaration, which automatically validates integer ranges
An xmlns:xs namespace declaration by itself
explanations: Correct. An XSD simple-type restriction can constrain an integer value with inclusive lower and upper facets such as xs:minInclusive and xs:maxInclusive.
xs:sequence controls the order and occurrence of child elements; it does not constrain an element's numeric value range.
#PCDATA declares parsed character data in a DTD; it does not provide this numeric range validation.
A namespace declaration associates a prefix with a namespace URI; it does not define datatype or value constraints.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus — p2-14 Web Technologies. W3C XML Schema 1.1 Part 2: Datatypes: https://www.w3.org/TR/2012/REC-xmlschema11-2-20120405/; W3C XML Schema 1.1 Part 1: https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema11-1/

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.subtopic: Java class initialization; superclass and instance initialization order
questions.stem: A Java program creates a Child object, where Child extends Parent. Assume neither class has been initialized, and each class has a static initialization block, an instance initialization block and a constructor that prints its class label. What is the order of the six labels?
options: Parent static, Child static, Parent instance, Parent constructor, Child instance, Child constructor
Child static, Parent static, Child instance, Parent instance, Child constructor, Parent constructor
Parent instance, Parent constructor, Parent static, Child static, Child instance, Child constructor
Parent static, Parent instance, Child static, Child instance, Parent constructor, Child constructor
explanations: Correct. Class initialization runs the superclass before the subclass. During object construction, superclass instance initializers run before the superclass constructor; only after that do the subclass instance initializers and constructor run.
The superclass is initialized before the subclass, and the superclass constructor runs before subclass instance initialization; this order reverses both rules.
Static class initialization must occur before instance construction, so the parent instance block cannot run first.
The parent constructor body runs before the child instance initializers; the listed order incorrectly places the child static block after parent instance initialization.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus — p2-15 OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA. Java Language Specification, Chapter 12, Execution (class initialization and instance creation): https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se7/html/jls-12.html
